response: Yes, aneurysm repair is justified for patients aged 80 or older after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. According to the study, better prognosis was obtained when ruptured aneurysm was repaired in the elderly than it was treated conservatively. Therefore, definitive surgery should not be withheld from elderly patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, and they should be offered the repair to improve their prognosis.
